chunks: Al-Sakūnī narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, said: “If a slave becomes blind, then there is no servitude upon him; and if a slave becomes leprous, then there is no servitude upon him.”

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the slave; the bonded person under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave becomes blind or leprous in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning a slave who becomes afflicted with severe bodily impairment such as blindness or leprosy. It states that in such a case, servitude no longer remains upon him, indicating a ruling tied to emancipation in these circumstances.
